decision: DIFFERS -> W1: author the page's figure. psu_ext elderberry-in-the-garden-and-the-kitchen states "Ensure spacing is 5 to 7 feet between plants" -> in_row [60,84]; no between-rows figure on any cited page (not_authored, as spec §10.1 expects). Today's [48,96] matches neither end on any cited page (MU AF1017's cached copy carries no spacing text; MSU and the NCSU toolbox give size only). The planting prose's '6 to 8 feet apart for full-size bushes' is re-authored to 5 to 7; its 4-ft hedge figure is a different layout and is left.

edits.new: Plant elderberry in late winter or early spring, at the same depth it was growing, in moist rich soil, and water it in. Give each plant room: about 4 feet apart for a hedge, or 5 to 7 feet apart for full-size bushes. Plant at least two different varieties near each other, and expect it to grow fast and send up suckers.
edits.reason: restates the moved in-row figure (PSU: 5 to 7 ft)

edits.new: Set dormant bare-root plants or rooted cuttings in late winter to early spring at the depth they grew, in moist, fertile soil, and water in well; container plants can go in spring or fall. Space plants about 4 feet apart in a hedge-style row, or 5 to 7 feet apart for full-size freestanding shrubs, with wider spacing between rows. Expect vigorous growth and suckering, and plan at least two cultivars for cross-pollination.
edits.reason: restates the moved in-row figure (PSU: 5 to 7 ft)

restatements.note: a sourcing record (cross-pollination within 60 ft), not a spacing restatement
